run.question: Database connection timeouts are occurring for blue-whale app in namespace app-94

report.summary: Fetched runbook skill_id=database-troubleshooting and carried out its steps with my own tools: (1) application status — Deployment blue-whale in app-94 is 1/1 ready and pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-855rs is Running, ready, restartCount 0; (2) logs — fetch_pod_logs returned no_data for the current container (0 lines, 0 bytes) and reported no previous container, so no application error lines were available to read; (3) database service/endpoints — Service postgres exists in app-94 (ClusterIP 10.96.43.247, port 5432, selector app=postgres-db), but its Endpoints object has subsets: null, i.e. zero addresses, and a cluster-wide pod query for app=postgres-db returned nothing; (4) network connectivity test — could not be executed (no exec facility among this Run's tools); (5) database health — not checkable because no postgres pod exists anywhere in the cluster; (6) connection-pool/config — read from the Deployment env: DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20. No NetworkPolicies and no ResourceQuotas exist in the cluster, and the only ConfigMap in app-94 is kube-root-ca.crt, so policy/quota blocking and ConfigMap-injected settings are not supported by the evidence. The deepest observable break is the postgres dependency: the Service that blue-whale is configured to dial has no endpoints because no workload labelled app=postgres-db exists in the cluster. Blue-whale's own timeout errors could not be corroborated: its container wrote no log lines, and every Prometheus and Jaeger query in this Run failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE / INVALID_PARAMS even though the prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy and jaeger pods are Running and ready. Change history is not integrated, so whether the postgres workload was deleted or never deployed is unknown; the conclusion is therefore partial.

claims.text: Deployment blue-whale in namespace app-94 has replicas=1, readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1, was created at 2026-11-23T16:36:30Z (managedFields: kubectl-client-side-apply Update at 2026-11-23T16:36:30Z, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1) and its container env is DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20.

Service postgres in namespace app-94 is a ClusterIP Service on port 5432 targeting port 5432 (clusterIP 10.96.43.247) with selector app=postgres-db, and the corresponding Endpoints object postgres in app-94 has subsets: null, i.e. no addresses or ports backed by any pod.

A cluster-wide pod query with label_selector app=postgres-db returned zero pods, and a scan of all 33 pods in the cluster found no pod whose name or labels indicate a postgres/database workload in any namespace (matches were limited to blue-whale and the otel-demo/kube-system workloads).

No postgres workload object exists: the only StatefulSet in the cluster is alertmanager in otel-demo, and the only Deployment whose name or labels match postgres/mysql/redis/valkey/db is valkey-cart in otel-demo; in app-94 the only Deployment is blue-whale (ready=1, available=1) with its single ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 owned by Deployment blue-whale.

No NetworkPolicies exist anywhere in the cluster and no ResourceQuotas exist anywhere in the cluster (both lists returned empty), and the only ConfigMap in app-94 is kube-root-ca.crt, which contains no DB connection or pool configuration.

Pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-855rs (owner ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5) is Running and ready, phase Running, restartCount 0, no last termination state, podIP 10.244.0.39, startTime 2026-11-23T16:36:30Z, running command python /app/app.py with code mounted from Secret blue-whale-app; the pod defines no readiness or liveness probe.

The only 6 events in the authorized window for the whole cluster are Normal lifecycle events at 2026-11-23T16:36:30Z for Pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-855rs (Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started), ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 (SuccessfulCreate) and Deployment blue-whale (ScalingReplicaSet, 'Scaled up replica set blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 from 0 to 1'); there is no SuccessfulDelete and no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Failed or Unhealthy event, and no event naming any postgres object.

The metrics and tracing backends are running as pods (prometheus-9bc78b5f7-k84v7, prometheus-readonly-proxy-7567c75596-nwrxw and jaeger-698d849b7b-qhlhm in otel-demo are Running and ready with restartCount 0), yet every Prometheus query (execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_prometheus_target) and traces_list_services/traces_search call in this Run returned status error SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (traces_search also INVALID_PARAMS for service blue-whale).

Likely cause of the reported database connection timeouts: blue-whale dials postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432, which resolves to Service postgres (10.96.43.247) whose Endpoints set is empty because no pod carrying label app=postgres-db exists in the cluster, so every connection attempt has no backend and can only fail or time out; the Service definition itself is present and the fault is the missing backing database endpoint.

Rejected: NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota blocking traffic from blue-whale to postgres. The cluster-wide NetworkPolicies list contains no objects at all and the cluster-wide ResourceQuotas list contains no objects, so no policy can be dropping these connections and no quota constrains app-94.

Rejected as far as observable: blue-whale failing through a crash loop, eviction or OOM. Its pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination state, it has no readiness/liveness probe to miss, and the window's events contain no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Failed or Unhealthy entries and no SuccessfulDelete.

Recommendation: restore a postgres workload in app-94 whose pods carry label app=postgres-db (so Service postgres acquires endpoints on 5432), or repoint DB_HOST/DB_PORT of Deployment blue-whale at a database that exists, then re-check Service postgres Endpoints and blue-whale's connection errors.

gaps: Validation of blue-whale's own timeout errors was not obtainable: fetch_pod_logs for pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-855rs returned status no_data (0 lines, 0 bytes read from the current container; no previous container existed), so its application error lines are unknown, not absent.

All Prometheus queries (up, kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="app-94"}, get_metric_names{namespace="app-94"}, get_label_values label=service_name, get_prometheus_target) and all Jaeger calls (traces_list_services, traces_search service=blue-whale) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE or INVALID_PARAMS, so no error-rate, latency or span evidence for blue-whale exists in this Run; the Jaeger service list also does not offer blue-whale as a service name.
fetch_pod_logs for otel-demo pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-7567c75596-nwrxw returned status no_data (0 lines, 0 bytes), so the proxy's own behaviour during the failed metric queries is unknown.

change_history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so whether a postgres workload previously existed in app-94 and was deleted, or was never deployed, cannot be determined; the postgres Service and all app-94 objects carry creationTimestamp 2026-11-23T16:36:30Z and no event mentions a postgres object.

The container code is mounted from Secret blue-whale-app, and secrets cannot be read, so blue-whale's retry/timeout behaviour (DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30) and its exact error text could not be verified.

Live connectivity test from the blue-whale pod to postgres:5432 (runbook step 4) and database health checks (runbook step 5, e.g. psql SELECT 1) could not be executed: no in-cluster exec/port-forward facility is available among this Run's tools, and there is no postgres pod to query in any case.
next_steps: Confirm with the application owner and secret blue-whale-app how blue-whale surfaces DB failures (timeout vs. connection refused) and whether the database is expected to run in-cluster.

Check cluster change history (not integrated here) for a deleted postgres Deployment/StatefulSet or PVC in app-94, or for the kubectl apply that introduced Service postgres with selector app=postgres-db.
When Prometheus is reachable again, verify blue-whale error/latency signals and kube_deployment_status_* for app-94, and re-run the runbook's Service/Endpoints check for postgres.
If a postgres workload is restored, verify Service postgres receives endpoints on 5432 and that blue-whale's connection errors stop.
